subject: pathology
title: Post-Streptococcal GN, Subepithelial Humps, and IgA Nephropathy Mesangial Deposits

steps.tx: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis follows nephritogenic streptococcal throat or skin infection by latent weeks, immune complexes swelling children with haematuria, oedema, hypertension, and low C3 recovering usually. That latent nephritis is **post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN)**. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions.
steps.say: Cola urine, swollen face, high pressure two weeks after strep throat in a child means PSGN.

steps.tx: Subepithelial humps, large immune deposits bulging beneath podocytes on electron microscopy with endocapillary neutrophils, sign postinfectious glomerulonephritis under glass. Those humps are the **subepithelial humps of postinfectious GN**. Examiners return to it because it separates careful clinicians from guesswork. Bedside recognition of this pattern saves time, blood, and unnecessary investigation.
steps.say: Humps on the epithelial side mean postinfectious deposits; neutrophils flooding capillaries agree.

steps.tx: IgA nephropathy deposits polymeric IgA in mesangium world wide, synpharyngitic haematuria arriving with sore throats within days, mesangial hypercellularity and Oxford scores staging progression. The mesangial disease is **IgA nephropathy (Berger disease)**. Students should anchor this fact before moving to rarer causes and exceptions.
steps.say: Visible blood with the sore throat, not weeks after, is IgA nephropathy signing its timing.

vis.caption: IgA nephropathy pathogenesis from galactose deficient IgA to mesangial deposits.

steps.tx: Galactose deficient IgA forms immune complexes with anti-glycan antibodies depositing mesangially and activating complement, a four hit model explaining familial and mucosal associations. That model is the **four-hit pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy**. In practice this distinction decides the next test, treatment, or referral made.
steps.say: Defective IgA sugar, anti-sugar antibodies, complexes, mesangial injury: IgA nephropathy in four hits.

steps.tx: IgA vasculitis, Henoch-Schonlein, shares mesangial IgA with systemic small vessel disease of skin, gut, and joints, kidney histology indistinguishable from IgA nephropathy. That systemic sibling is **IgA vasculitis nephritis versus IgA nephropathy**. That is why this detail earns its place in every examination and ward round.
steps.say: Palpable purpura plus mesangial IgA is IgA vasculitis; kidney alone keeps the nephropathy name.

vis.caption: Proliferative glomerulonephritis patterns across postinfectious, IgA, and lupus diseases.

steps.tx: Persistent low C3 beyond eight to twelve weeks after apparent PSGN rewrites differential toward C3 glomerulopathy or lupus, demanding biopsy rather than continued reassurance. That deadline is **persistent hypocomplementaemia after postinfectious GN**. Remembering it prevents the commonest errors made with this presentation entirely.
steps.say: C3 still low at twelve weeks is not slow PSGN recovery; biopsy toward C3 disease or lupus.

steps.tx: Supportive care, salt restriction, diuretics, pressure control, and streptococcal eradication treat most childhood PSGN without immunosuppression unless crescents supervene. Restraint defines **supportive management of post-streptococcal GN**. The clinical payoff comes from applying it early, before complications accumulate further. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions.
steps.say: Most childhood PSGN needs diuretics, salt sense, and time, not steroids; crescents change that.

steps.tx: IgA nephropathy therapy now layers optimised RAAS and SGLT2 support, targeted budesonide for intestinal immune modulation, and trials for high risk proteinuria despite support. That layering is **contemporary IgA nephropathy therapy**. Examiners return to it because it separates careful clinicians from guesswork.
steps.say: Support first, then gut targeted budesonide and trials select IgA patients still leaking protein.
